title: Philosophy / Point of view

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; interactive elements retain their captured state

slide_intent: Define the human relationship behind design decisions, because consistency needs a purpose beyond repeating recognizable shapes.
strategic_value: Linking IBM’s role between people and machines to guidance can give teams a common reason to preserve both usefulness and character.
demonstration: A film player precedes a long-form argument about building bonds, design heritage, the relationship between mankind and machine, and the Think → Guide ethos.
practical_value: Evaluate an expression by how it guides people and represents IBM’s character, rather than by visual resemblance alone.

content_islands.name: Title and film
content_islands.spec: Open with the black Point of view header and the wide film player showing a typographic guide frame.

content_islands.name: Build bonds argument
content_islands.spec: Place the introductory purpose statement above the Design is how we build bonds section; retain the small design-history sidebar.

content_islands.name: Aesthetic and distinction
content_islands.spec: Follow with the Paul Rand quotation and the Stand for = Stand out argument, paired with the Here → There note.

content_islands.name: Think → Guide
content_islands.spec: End the essay with enduring criteria for anyone designing on IBM’s behalf and the time-saved or time-well-spent sidebar.

reference_purposes.Intent: The essay explicitly connects design to relationships, progress and guiding people emotionally and functionally.
reference_purposes.Application: The closing section presents philosophy and principles as criteria for anyone authoring or authorizing IBM design.
